studies.title: SOMA Inspiration4 Blood Serum Multiplex Cytokine and Chemokine Profiling
studies.description: Comprehensive metabolic panel and multiplex cytokine/chemokine profiling from four commercial astronauts aboard the Inspiration4 mission (3-day low-Earth orbit, apogee ~585 km). Tracks circulating inflammatory, cardiac stress, and metabolic adaptation markers pre-flight, immediately post-flight, and across long-term recovery.
studies.mission_context: Inspiration4 Commercial Crew Mission (Crew Dragon Resilience, 3 days LEO)
studies.measurements_summary: Plasma cytokines (IL-6, TNF-alpha, VEGF), electrolytes, BUN, creatinine, troponin, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP).
studies.publication_citation: Beheshti, A., Mason, C. E., et al. (2024). The Space Omics and Medical Atlas (SOMA) accelerates space medicine. Nature, 632, 1158-1172.
studies.limitations: Commercial civilian crew (N=4) on a short 3-day low-Earth orbit mission; transient metabolic and inflammatory shifts cannot establish chronic deep-space clinical pathology thresholds.

studies.title: Single-Cell RNA-seq, snATAC-seq, and Immune Repertoires of Inspiration4 Crew
studies.description: Single-cell and single-nucleus multi-omic characterization of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from the 4-member Inspiration4 crew. Details transient immune dysregulation, T-cell receptor (TCR) clonality shifts, and gene expression recovery kinetics.
studies.mission_context: Inspiration4 Commercial Crew Mission (Crew Dragon Resilience, 3 days LEO)
studies.measurements_summary: Single-cell transcriptome counts across 18 PBMC sub-populations, chromatin accessibility peaks, and V(D)J immune receptor clonal frequencies.
studies.publication_citation: Mason, C. E., et al. (2024). Single-cell immune repertoire profiling of civilian spaceflight astronauts. Nature, 632, 1173-1185.
studies.limitations: Short-duration commercial flight; single-cell PBMC transcriptomic adaptations do not equate to clinical immune deficiency or opportunistic infection.

studies.title: PlanHab: Combined and Separate Effects of 21 Days Bed Rest and Hypoxic Confinement on Human Skeletal Muscle miRNA Expression
studies.description: Ground-based microgravity simulation using horizontal and head-down tilt (-6 degree HDT) bed rest with normobaric hypoxia (PlanHab) to investigate muscle unloading, fiber atrophy, and recovery in healthy human subjects.
studies.mission_context: Ground-based Head-Down Tilt Bed Rest Study (-6 deg HDT, 21 days)
studies.measurements_summary: Vastus lateralis muscle biopsy mRNA and miRNA expression, slow-to-fast twitch fiber type shifts, and cross-sectional area changes.
studies.publication_citation: NASA Human Research Program & ESA Bed Rest Studies Consortium.
studies.limitations: Terrestrial ground bed rest analog with normobaric hypoxia; lacks actual microgravity cephalad fluid redistribution and space radiation.

studies.title: Large-scale mRNA analysis of female skeletal muscles during 60 days of bed rest with and without exercise or dietary protein supplementation as countermeasures
studies.description: Evaluates skeletal muscle gene expression in female subjects undergoing prolonged 60-day head-down tilt bed rest with nutritional and resistive/aerobic exercise countermeasures (WISE-2005).
studies.mission_context: WISE-2005 60-day Female Bed Rest Study (Toulouse, France)
studies.measurements_summary: Soleus and vastus lateralis transcriptome shifts, proteolysis pathways, and countermeasure efficacy metrics.
studies.publication_citation: Edgerton, V. R., et al. (2007). Human muscle adaptation to bed rest and exercise countermeasures.
studies.limitations: Terrestrial ground analog in healthy female volunteers; reflects horizontal bed rest disuse in Earth gravity, not 3D microgravity vestibular and radiation environment.

studies.title: Human Skeletal Muscle Tissue Chip Autonomous Payload on the ISS
studies.description: Autonomous 3D human skeletal muscle myobundle tissue chip flown on the International Space Station (SpaceX CRS-21) to model microgravity-induced sarcopenia, sarcomeric disorganization, and metabolic gene alterations.
studies.mission_context: ISS National Laboratory Expedition 64 (SpaceX CRS-21, 10 days microgravity)
studies.measurements_summary: Myotube diameter, twitch force kinetics, and RNA-Seq differential expression of sarcomeric and mitochondrial genes.
studies.publication_citation: Soman, P., et al. (2023). Microgravity-induced sarcopenia modeling using human muscle-on-a-chip. npj Microgravity, 9, 45.
studies.limitations: In vitro engineered 3D muscle microtissues; lacks vascular perfusion, systemic neural innervation, and whole-body endocrine feedback.

studies.title: Spaceflight Effects on Human Vascular Smooth Muscle Cell Phenotype and Function
studies.description: Investigates phenotypic modulation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and vascular contractility in human primary vascular smooth muscle cells cultured aboard the International Space Station.
studies.measurements_summary: Alpha-SMA contractility markers, collagen/elastin turnover gene expression, and endothelial adhesion molecules.
studies.publication_citation: NASA Space Biology Program, Ames Research Center.
studies.limitations: In vitro 2D cell culture without pulsatile hemodynamic pressure, endothelial shear stress, or autonomic baroreceptor control.

studies.title: T Cell Activation in Microgravity Compared to 1g (Earth's) Gravity Study
studies.description: Flown on Space Shuttle Discovery (STS-131) and the ISS; demonstrates that microgravity significantly inhibits immediate early gene expression and protein kinase C (PKC) signaling cascades during human T-cell activation.
studies.measurements_summary: IL-2 transcription, c-jun/c-fos induction levels, and T-cell mitogenic responsiveness in microgravity vs 1g centrifuge control.
studies.publication_citation: Hughes-Fulford, M., et al. (2005). Microgravity inhibits immediate early gene expression in T-cells. FASEB J, 19, 1311-1313.
studies.limitations: In vitro isolated cell cultures stimulated artificially with concanavalin A; does not capture in vivo lymphoid organ architecture or complex immune response in astronauts.

studies.title: Transcriptomic Effects on the Mouse Heart Following 30 Days on the International Space Station Study
studies.description: Evaluates left ventricular myocardial remodeling, cytoskeletal organization, and mitochondrial energetics in mice flown for 30 days aboard the International Space Station (Rodent Research-12).
studies.mission_context: ISS Rodent Research-12 (RR-12 / TARBIS, 30 days on ISS)
studies.measurements_summary: Ventricular myocardial RNA-Seq counts, titin/myosin heavy chain ratios, and cardiac oxidative phosphorylation enzyme profiles.
studies.publication_citation: NASA Space Biology Program, Ames Research Center.
studies.limitations: Murine model with basal heart rate of ~600 bpm and predominantly alpha-MHC myocardium (unlike beta-MHC dominant human heart); cannot set human cardiac clinical thresholds.

studies.title: Mighty Mice in Space: Pre-clinical Evaluation of a Broad Spectrum Myostatin Inhibitor to Prevent Muscle and Bone Loss Due to Disuse
studies.description: Rodent Research-19 (RR-19) spaceflight study evaluating systemic administration of ACVR2B/Fc decoy receptor in mice to prevent microgravity-induced musculoskeletal loss.
studies.mission_context: ISS Rodent Research-19 (SpaceX CRS-19, 33 days on ISS)
studies.measurements_summary: Trabecular and cortical volumetric bone mineral density (femur/tibia), soleus/gastrocnemius wet weights, and circulating myostatin levels.
studies.publication_citation: Lee, S. J., et al. (2020). Targeting myostatin/activin A protects against skeletal muscle and bone loss during spaceflight. PNAS, 117(39), 24411-24419.
studies.limitations: Pre-clinical murine study using genetic knockouts and experimental decoy receptor ACVR2B/Fc; therapeutic agent is not FDA-approved for human spaceflight countermeasures.

studies.title: Transcriptional analysis of dorsal skin from mice flown on the RR-7 mission
studies.description: Transcriptional profiling of dorsal skin tissue from mice flown on the International Space Station for 30 days during the Rodent Research-7 (RR-7) mission, investigating microgravity and spaceflight environment effects on mammalian cutaneous tissue and epidermal barrier maintenance.
studies.mission_context: ISS Rodent Research-7 (SpaceX CRS-15, 30 days on ISS)
studies.measurements_summary: Dorsal skin mRNA transcript expression, extracellular matrix turnover markers, and epidermal barrier regulatory genes.
studies.publication_citation: Vitaterna, M. H., Turek, F. W., et al. (2020) / Rodent Research-7 (RR-7).
studies.limitations: Murine rodent model with furred integument; dorsal skin transcriptional responses cannot be directly equated with human astronaut epidermal barrier changes or clinical dermatological conditions.

studies.title: Transcription profiling of rat response to changes in developmental stage - 3 types of tissue, 3 gravity conditions, 2 developmental conditions
studies.description: Comparative transcription profiling of rat mammary gland, liver, and adipose tissues across microgravity (STS-66 flight), terrestrial 1g control, and hypergravity (centrifuge) conditions across developmental transitions. Investigates mechanotransduction and tissue homeorhesis; circadian regulatory pathways are analyzed as broader physiological context.
studies.mission_context: Space Shuttle STS-66 (NIH.R2 Payload, 11 days LEO)
studies.measurements_summary: Differential mRNA transcript abundance across mammary gland, liver, and adipose tissues under varying gravitational loads and reproductive/developmental stages.
studies.publication_citation: Casey, T., Patel, O. V., & Plaut, K. (2015). Transcriptomes reveal alterations in gravity impact circadian clocks and activate mechanotransduction pathways. Physiol Genomics, 47(5), 140-152.
studies.limitations: Evaluated in lactating and developing female rat models under acute gravitational shifts; physiological homeorhesis and tissue-specific responses cannot be used to establish human operational thresholds.

studies.title: Combined space stressors induce independent behavioral deficits predicted by early peripheral blood monocytes (Behavioral Assays)
studies.description: Evaluates the combined triad of deep-space hazards: 33-beam simulated galactic cosmic radiation (SimGCRsim, 500 mGy), prolonged social isolation, and hindlimb unloading in murine models at NSRL.
studies.mission_context: NASA Space Radiation Laboratory (NSRL) Ground Simulation Analog
studies.measurements_summary: Elevated Plus Maze anxiety index, Novel Object Recognition discrimination ratio, Morris Water Maze latency, and plasma IL-1beta/IL-6.
studies.publication_citation: Krukowski, K., Rosi, S., et al. (2021). Synergistic effects of space radiation and environmental stressors. Nat Commun, 12, 3941.
studies.limitations: Terrestrial NSRL accelerator simulation with acute ion beams; rodent behavioral anxiety paradigms cannot determine astronaut operational cognitive flight status.

studies.title: Differential Impact of Social Isolation and Space Radiation on Behavior and Motor Learning in Rats
studies.description: Tests how social isolation housing and fractionated ion-beam irradiation independently and interactively impair rotarod motor learning, exploratory vigor, and neuroendocrine stress hormones.
studies.mission_context: NASA Space Radiation Laboratory (NSRL) Mars Transit Confinement Simulation
studies.measurements_summary: Rotarod fall latency, balance beam foot faults, open-field center occupancy time, and plasma corticosterone concentrations.
studies.publication_citation: Adkins, A., Colby, E., Boden, A., Gotthold, J., Harris, R., Britten, R., Wellman, L., Sanford, L. (2023). Differential Impact of Social Isolation and Space Radiation on Behavior and Motor Learning in Rats. Life, 13(7), 1540.
studies.limitations: Single-housed rodent model under terrestrial particle beam irradiation; cannot model human astronaut crew cohesion, psychological selection, or cognitive mission training.

studies.title: Low-dose Simulated Galactic Cosmic Radiation Exposure After Hindlimb Unloading Has Long-term Impact on Skeletal Muscle Metabolic Proteins
studies.description: Quantitative proteomic profiling of murine skeletal muscle evaluating long-term persistent metabolic remodeling 9 months after exposure to hindlimb unloading and low-dose simulated galactic cosmic radiation at NSRL.
studies.mission_context: NASA Space Radiation Laboratory (NSRL) GCRsim + Hindlimb Unloading (9-month recovery)
studies.measurements_summary: Abundance changes in mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation complexes, fatty acid beta-oxidation enzymes, and structural sarcomeric proteins 9 months post-exposure.
studies.publication_citation: NASA Space Radiation Program Element, Human Research Program (GLDS-797).
studies.limitations: Murine ground analog model combining acute accelerator radiation and unloading with sedentary recovery; long-term proteomic alterations cannot directly define human post-flight muscle rehabilitation timelines.

studies.title: The impact of deep space radiation on cognitive performance: From biological sex to biomarkers to countermeasures
studies.description: Evaluates sex-dimorphic neurological vulnerability, persistent microglial activation, and cognitive performance deficits in mice following low-dose galactic cosmic radiation at NSRL.
studies.mission_context: NASA Space Radiation Laboratory (NSRL) Galactic Cosmic Ray Simulation
studies.measurements_summary: Barnes maze primary latency and search errors, Iba-1 positive microglial cell counts, and hippocampal cytokine transcript levels.
studies.publication_citation: Rosi, S., et al. (2020). Sex-specific cognitive deficits following galactic cosmic ray exposure. Science Advances, 6(42), eabb9379.
studies.limitations: Terrestrial ground simulation using acute GCRsim beam; rodent spatial learning latencies do not correlate directly with human flight certification criteria.
